root.name: Queen's Pawn Game: Barry Attack
root.moves: 1. d4 d5 2. Nc3 Nf6 3. Nf3 g6 4. Bf4

overview: White develops Nc3, Nf3 and Bf4 against Black's ...g6 and ...d5 set-up, a London-like build-up that avoids main-line Grünfeld and King's Indian theory. The usual plan is e3, Be2, h3 and 0-0 with pressure on d5 and e5, while Black replies with ...Bg7, ...O-O and ...c5 or ...Nc6. The Tarzan Attack with Qd2 and Bh6 is a sharper side branch.

white_ideas.idea: Develop Nf3, Nc3, Bf4, e3 and Be2 without committing the c-pawn
Trade Black's fianchettoed bishop with Qd2 and Bh6 in the Tarzan Attack

black_ideas.idea: Fianchetto with ...Bg7 and castle, then strike with ...c5 or ...Nc6 and ...e5 ideas
Pressure d4 and use the queenside majority to equalise

typical_structures.structure: d4/e3 against d5/g6 fianchetto, London-like with the bishop on f4

character.notes: Main line is a steady development; only the Tarzan Attack brings forcing play.

soundness.notes: A respectable set-up, if lacking sting.

structure.notes: Tension between d4 and d5 with undecided centre, like the London.

approach.notes: A development scheme White uses against ...g6/...d5 set-ups, with plans mattering more than move order.

level.notes: Few forcing lines, but it is a less standard set-up than the London.

sublines_that_differ.name: Tarzan Attack
sublines_that_differ.how: White aims for Bh6 and a kingside attack; sharper than the main line.

character.reason: Development-led play without forcing lines, though Black has active counterplay.

structure.reason: The d4/d5 centre stays in tension, as in the London.

approach.reason: A set-up played against ...g6 and ...d5 where plans matter more than move order.

level.reason: Easy to learn but Black's active replies need judgement.

plans.reason: No plan from the table characterises the main line clearly.
